payload.headline: NVIDIA: reported CEO turmoil and China curbs weigh; the 2026-11-17 report decides

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast with very high margins and trades below most fair-value estimates, but leadership turmoil, new reported China limits and an earnings report right away make the near term hard to call.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, no adding before the 2026-11-17 report; no swing trade until that report is out.
summary.act_at: Hold at 162.85; add near 151.37 only after a clean report; reassess near 224.74

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 162.85, down 2.01% on the day. It is in a downtrend and below its 20-day (198.69), 50-day (214.63) and 200-day (203.92) averages. News since the last note is about Jensen Huang's reported exit as CEO, with reported calls from investors and the tech world for his return. Separately, Commerce is reported to be closing a third-country loophole that let China use NVIDIA computing power. The first earnings report under CFO Colette Kress is due on 2026-11-17.
payload.business: The latest numbers are very strong. Quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after investment) reached 127.0B over the last year, up from 72.0B. The company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. The leadership news mainly hits sentiment and governance for now. It does not change last quarter's sales or cash. Losing a founder-CEO can affect strategy and customer relationships over time (general knowledge), but nothing in DATA measures that yet. Three things could change the business itself. First, the reported Commerce crackdown on the China loophole could cut some demand. Second, unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which may mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Third, the 65% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and peaks like that usually fade. What is not at risk in the short run is the balance sheet: liquidity is 56.6B and the company is buying back shares, with shares outstanding down 1.01% from a year earlier.

worth.text: At 162.85 the stock trades at 20.5 times last year's earnings, 17.5 times this year's estimate and 10.3 times next year's estimate. Its price-to-sales ratio (price compared with yearly sales) is 13.0. That is below the peer median of 16.6 and in only the 9.0 percentile of its own 5-year history. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 193.13 / 224.74 / 267.17 for bear / base / bull. The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 217.35 to 411.04. The two methods differ mainly because the cash-flow model caps starting growth at 30% even though sales grew 83%, while the history method assumes the market will pay past multiples again. Today's price implies starting cash-flow growth of 21.9% a year. At 20% growth the value is 151.37; at 30% it is 220.46. The biggest swing factor is margin. If operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 113.77, and at 32% it drops to 76.17. My range runs from 151.37, which assumes slower growth, to 224.74, the base case. That range is lower than the automated summary because the margin is at a peak.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%.

bull: Cheap if forecasts hold: 10.3 times next-year earnings. Analysts raised next-year EPS 23.7% over 90 days to 15.85.
Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago, and free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B.
Valued below peers and its own past: price-to-sales of 13.0 against a peer median of 16.6, at the 9.0 percentile of its 5-year range.
bear: Margins are at a peak. Operating margin of 65.21% is the top of its 5-year range, and at 48% the value model gives only 113.77.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% against sales growth of 106%, which may mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched.
Leadership upheaval and a reported China crackdown hit a stock already in a downtrend, below its 50-day average of 214.63. Put/call open interest is 1.51 (more bets on a fall than a rise).

levels.what: Today's close. It sits inside the 151.37–224.74 range and implies 21.9% starting cash-flow growth. That is enough to keep holding but not enough to add, given the leadership turmoil and earnings in one day.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only if the 2026-11-17 report shows operating margin near 65% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
Base-case cash-flow value. Near this price most of the valuation upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee says 'Hold', and the technical, macro and risk views are all negative. Strong numbers support owning the stock. Unclear leadership and a report that can move the price sharply argue against adding now.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend with no support level below the price and resistance just above at 163.9–169.14. Options price a 10.3% move by 2026-11-20, against an ATR (average daily range) of 9.98, so the report can jump past any stop.

decision.timing: No action before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 81.0 against 54.0 realized (1.5x) shows the market expects a big move. After the report, check this quarter's revenue against the 108.7B estimate, the operating margin, and how fast customer bills are growing compared with sales.

change_mind: Turn to wait or avoid: the 2026-11-17 report shows revenue below the 108.7B estimate or EPS below 2.47, or operating margin falling from 65.21% toward 48%.
Add: the price falls to 151.37 after a report that keeps margin near 65% and shows customer-bill growth back in line with sales.
Re-open a swing entry: the price closes above the 169.91–175.15 resistance zone, which would break the pattern of lower highs.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold, because the reported Commerce crackdown on the China loophole and growing calls for Huang's return added risk without changing the numbers, while the valuation levels moved slightly (154.19 to 151.37, 228.42 to 224.74).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
